newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arab ministers approve boycott resolution on Israel.
newsitem.headline: Arab ministers approve boycott resolution on Israel.

text.p: Arab foreign ministers recommended on Monday that Arab states put an end to normal relations with Israel and restore the economic boycott.
Arab League Secretary General Esmat Abdel-Meguid read out the resolution after the foreign ministers ended two days of talks dominated by Israel's attitude to Middle East peace.
"The Arab League recommended this and this is binding. All members are obliged to stick to the resolution," he added.

"It's a message to Israel and to the leader of Israel but the main thrust of this is to save the peace process. They (the Israelis) have totally miscalculated the Arab reaction and this is something that should never have happened," he said.

The decision is the strongest concerted step the Arab states have taken since rightwing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu took office last year on a platform that challenged what Arabs saw as the basic principles of peace talks.
The immediate stimulus was Arab anger at Netanyahu's decision this month to go ahead with a Jewish settlement at Jabal Abu Ghneim, or Har Homa, in Arab East Jerusalem despite Arab objections.
"Netanyahu is playing with fire and the first person to be burnt by this will be him," Abdel-Meguid said.
"It's Netanyahu who started and he who starts is the one who's in the wrong. Let the people of Israel call him to account. This is a serious situation," he added.
"They've miscalculated the Islamic and Christian reaction and if they think that by the Jabal Abu Ghneim settlement they are putting Arabs to the test then this is the answer," he said.
"This decision was adopted unanimously. We're talking about a very clear text. This decision was worded carefully and all sides especially the Israeli must understand the meaning."
The resolution also recommends that Arab states close down any Israeli offices and missions and withdraw from multilateral talks on aspects of Middle East peace.
But it does not affect Egypt, Jordan and the Palestinians, who have signed formal peace agreements with Israel.
Abdel-Meguid told the news conference that the resolution was also a message to the United States, which has vetoed two U.N. Security Council resolutions critical of Israel this month.
"The Arab world is very upset by the two vetoes and this is the most serious U.S. action... We are against the settlement because it stands against peace," he said.
"We say to our friends in Europe and America that we are advocates of peace but the Arab nation will never surrender."
